answers.A: Principle of Least Privilege — ensuring the camera unit only accesses data necessary for its function, such as terrain maps but not passenger biometrics.
answers.B: Principle of Complete Mediation — requiring every access to camera data to be validated through a centralized security gateway before processing.
answers.C: Principle of Isolation — enforcing strict separation between the camera perception unit and other subsystems (e.g., telematics, dispatch logic) to prevent unintended data leakage or control interference.
answers.D: Principle of Fail-safe Defaults — configuring the system to deny all access unless explicitly permitted, defaulting to safe behavior if perception fails.
